title: Batista2022
description: EEG recordings from 20 healthy volunteers performing cued left- versus right-hand motor imagery of a bimanual rowing task during brain-computer interface training. The study compared Graz and NeuRow virtual-reality conditions with optional haptic and head-mounted-display feedback. Peripheral physiological signals (ECG, respiration, PPG, accelerometry) were also recorded. This version is a BIDS-formatted derivative of the Zenodo deposit, prepared for use with MOABB.
methods_description: 32-channel EEG was recorded at 500 Hz with a Brain Products LiveAmp 32 and actiCAP active Ag/AgCl electrodes (10-20 montage), together with ECG, respiration and auxiliary channels. Each subject completed one session with up to five imagery runs (MI, MIMO, MIMOHP, MIMOVR, MIMOVRHP), each trial having a 5 s cue-locked imagery/feedback window.
